answer.text: The monetary value of a society's physical infrastructure
Networks together with shared norms, values and understandings that facilitate cooperation within or among groups
The GDP of a country divided by population
The total sum of philanthropic capital raised in a given year

explanation.text: The Logic: Per p21 (Ch 1.5.1), the OECD defines Social Capital as 'networks together with shared norms, values and understandings that facilitate cooperation within or among groups'. The World Bank provides a complementary definition on the same page. The Trap: Option A confuses with physical capital. Option C is per-capita GDP. Option D confuses with philanthropic capital. Note: Social capital is a cross-cutting theme across many SE programmes; the OECD wording on p21 is the source-supported definition for the AIR.
